subject: Clarify inclusion criteria for hosting environments (SIG questionnaire)
messages:
From: Alex Torres <atorres@finco.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: FinCo Security <security@finco.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: SIG questions: which hosting modes to include in PT report?

Hi Kimberly,

Apologies for the rapid follow-up — our risk team is completing the SIG questionnaire and the item around penetration testing scope is ambiguous. Can you confirm which of the following hosting modes Redwood considers "in-scope" for your standard PT artifacts or SOC2 evidence?

- Hosted API (Redwood fully managed, multi-tenant hosted endpoints)
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools reserved for a single customer but managed by Redwood)
- Private / VPC (control plane in Redwood, data plane inside customer VPC)
- On-prem (customer-installed bundle)

We need to map evidence to our SIG answers and to the procurement checklist. I attached our current SIG excerpt with the questions highlighted. If you have a short inclusion matrix you can share, that would be ideal.

Also please let us know whether Redwood would run an external pen test (from an approved vendor) across customer VPCs for Private deployments or if that needs to be coordinated by the customer.

Thanks — if easier we can jump on a quick call.

Alex Torres
Senior InfoSec Manager, FinCo
atorres@finco.com

Attachment: finco_SIG_questions_v3.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <atorres@finco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG questions: which hosting modes to include in PT report?

Hi Alex — thanks for sending this over. Short answer: the inclusion depends on the deployment model and the tenancy boundary. Below are quick bullets; I'll pull together a concise matrix and authorization template and loop in our PT vendor if you want Redwood to run the test.

- Hosted API: Redwood-managed, multi-tenant; our public PT reports cover the runtime and control plane we operate. For customer-specific assurance we can provide SOC2 evidence and a summary of pen test findings (redacted).
- Dedicated: typically Redwood-managed infrastructure dedicated to one customer. We consider the Redwood-managed GPU pools and control plane in-scope for Redwood's PT reports. Anything running inside the customer's network or customer-managed agents is out-of-scope unless explicitly included by engagement.
- Private / VPC: control plane remains Redwood-hosted; data plane sits in the customer's VPC. The split means Redwood's PT covers our control plane components and any managed connectors; the customer's VPC and customer-managed hosts are usually the customer's responsibility. We can coordinate a vendor test inside the VPC, but we'll need customer auth and network access.
- On-prem: customer-installed package; out-of-scope for Redwood PTs. Customers are responsible for their own assessments.

Can you confirm which model your deployment uses? Also, do you want Redwood to manage the vendor engagement (we typically work with BoxSec for these types of VPC tests) or do you prefer to run your own contractor?

I'll draft a one-page inclusion matrix and a short authorization template and send shortly.

Kimberly Park
Principal, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Kim / Laura — adding detail so Kimberly has language to share with FinCo. Feel free to copy/paste these bullets into the inclusion matrix.

- Hosted API: Covered by our public PT and SOC2 scope; share summary and redacted findings.
- Dedicated: In-scope for Redwood PT when the capacity is "Redwood Dedicated" (i.e., GPU hosts, hypervisor, network managed by Redwood as part of a reserved capacity contract). Customer applications running on top of the dedicated capacity under a customer-managed control plane are out-of-scope unless we agree otherwise in the SOW.
- Private / VPC: Split scope. Redwood's control plane services (auth, model routing, billing) are in-scope for Redwood. Data-plane systems (customer VMs, private KMS endpoints, customer-managed networking) are in-scope for the customer's assessments. If FinCo asks Redwood to sponsor a vendor test inside their VPC, BoxSec will need an authorization letter and network access (bastion or temporary rules).
- On-prem: Out-of-scope.

Notes:
- For Dedicated and Private we typically provide a two-part artifact: (1) Redwood PT summary + SOC2 mapping; (2) a recommended customer checklist for the VPC/on-prem components they must validate.
- If FinCo requires Redwood to run the vendor test inside the VPC, procurement needs to approve a limited-scope SOW; we should match the SIG questions to the SOW so the vendor can test precisely what FinCo needs.

Vivek — can you confirm the list of approved vendors and the standard authorization language? Laura, I added you for contract coordination.

Rishi
Director, Product Security

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. I've attached two artifacts: an inclusion matrix that maps the four hosting modes to what Redwood covers by default, and a short authorization template you can use to provision a vendor in your VPC.

Key actionable items and next steps:
1) Confirm your deployment model (Hosted / Dedicated / Private-VPC / On-prem). If Private-VPC, please confirm whether FinCo wants Redwood to coordinate the vendor engagement (BoxSec) or whether you'll engage your own supplier.
2) If you want Redwood to coordinate, please: (a) sign the attached authorization template, (b) provide network access details (bastion IP or ephemeral rule window), and (c) provide the primary technical contact for FinCo (SSH/jump hostname, point-of-contact).
3) If you prefer to run your own vendor, we'll provide a Redwood test-playbook excerpt and sample artifact mapping to the SIG responses.

I've copied BoxSec (our preferred external testing partner) so they see the ask. BoxSec — if you can share your standard scope-of-work (network vs app tests) and availability for May-June windows, we can propose dates.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 20-minute sync if that speeds things up.

Regards,

Kimberly Park
